content: import { FDOSDK, FDOInterface, PluginMetadata, defineRenderOnLoadActions } from '@anikitenko/fdo-sdk'; // Import the rendering composition entry. /index.ts must remain a thin plugin entry that delegates the full workbench markup to /render.tsx. import { renderShell, renderOnLoad } from './render'; // Import the actions module so the entry can pass the returned action object through renderOnLoad. // The /render.tsx module also re-exports or exposes the action bindings through its renderOnLoad function. // This keeps the entry free of direct DOM interaction. export class WebToolsWorkbenchPlugin extends FDOSDK implements FDOInterface { // Keep the SDK metadata stable so the deployed plugin surfaces the intended name and verified BlueprintJS icon. private readonly metadata: PluginMetadata = { name: 'Web Tools Workbench', version: '1.0.0', author: 'Web Tools', description: 'A local, browser-only dashboard for compact webmaster and developer utilities.', icon: 'applications' }; // Required SDK metadata accessor. get metadata(): PluginMetadata { return this.metadata; } // Lifecycle entry point. The workbench UI is fully browser-local and deterministic, so no backend handler is registered here. // Keeping init() empty avoids host capability requirements and matches the installed SDK pattern for simple UI plugins. init(): void { this.info('Web Tools Workbench initialized', { plugin: this.metadata.name, version: this.metadata.version }); } // Return the rendered workbench HTML string. This is the only markup emitted by the backend; all interaction happens inside the iframe. render(): string { return renderShell(); } // The SDK expects an executable action bundle for iframe bindings. Delegate to the composition entry so all button listeners are defined in one place. renderOnLoad() { return renderOnLoad(); } } // Explicitly instantiate the plugin at module scope so the deployed plugin starts after import. const plugin = new WebToolsWorkbenchPlugin(); export default plugin;
